capitals.name: Guishan (Kuishan; Khujand in the page's brackets); Ershi in the Han accounts of the siege
capitals.note: 'The capital of the kingdom of Dayuan is the city of Guishan' (Zhang Qian, c. 128 BCE); the War of the Heavenly Horses page has Li Guangli laying siege to 'Ershi' in 102-101 BC. The page does not settle whether these are one city; coordinates are Khujand's, approximate.

correction.text: Dayuan, the Ferghana valley with its seventy walled cities

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -128..-111, no Cliopatria shape: Zhang Qian described Dayuan 'around 128 BCE' (mentioned in 130 BCE) as a kingdom of 60,000 families, 300,000 people, 60,000 trained troops and 'fully seventy' walled cities, 'generally accepted as relating to the Ferghana Valley' (the page's 'southwestern part of the Ferghana valley' is said of Alexandria Eschate (reviewer ia-01-b, 2026-10-18)). The -110 shape (51 k km2) is carried back eighteen years. Cliopatria's Yuezhi shape of -126..-111 contains the Ferghana basin (42 k km2 of overlap), which the Dayuan page contradicts.

-110..-64, 50,986 km2 (68.9-73.0 E, 39.7-41.7 N): the Ferghana valley. The page has no infobox area; Zhang Qian's 300,000 people and seventy cities fit a basin of this size. 'Dayuan becomes a puppet-state of Han' after 101 BC (War of the Heavenly Horses infobox) without a change of land.
-63..-51, 50,939 km2. Unchanged; the pages are silent for these years (unverified).

-50..42, 51,348 km2. Unchanged; unverified for the period. The Kangju page: 'By this time [the Hanshu's span, 206 BCE-23 CE] it had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana' (undated), which the shape does not show.

43..50, 51,348 km2, the last Great Yuan shape; Cliopatria's Kushan Empire shape of 51 covers it. The Kushan page opened says nothing on Ferghana, so the end in 50 is unverified (ledger 50, confidence 1).

region.text: Dayuan, the Ferghana valley with its seventy walled cities

ledger.note: 128 BC: Zhang Qian finds the kingdom of Dayuan in Ferghana. 'When the Chinese explorer Zhang Qian described Dayuan around 128 BCE' (also 'mentioned ... in 130 BCE'): 60,000 families, 300,000 people, 60,000 trained troops, 'fully seventy' walled cities, the capital Guishan. The page gives no founding (Alexander took Ferghana in 329 BCE; Seleucid until 250 BCE; Saka invasion c. 160 BCE); this is the first dated account of the state. Cliopatria's row starts in -110.

region.text: Ershi and the cities of the Ferghana valley, besieged by the Han

ledger.note: 102 BC: Li Guangli's second army reaches Dayuan. 'In the autumn of 102 BC, Li set out with an army of 60,000'; 'Upon arriving at Ershi, Li immediately laid siege to it' and, 'After a forty-day siege', broke the outer wall and cut the water. The first expedition (autumn 104 BC) had been beaten at Yucheng and retreated to Dunhuang.

region.text: Ershi and the Ferghana valley after the peace of 101 BC

ledger.note: 101 BC: the nobles of Dayuan kill their king and buy peace. 'First they killed their king, Wugua'; 'Li agreed to the terms, taking some 3,000 horses as well as provisions' and 'enthroned one of the nobles called Meicai as king'. Infobox: 'Dayuan becomes a puppet-state of Han.' The page gives the campaign as 102-101 BC and no month; the Kangju page has Kangju 'helping them preserve their independence against the Han' in 101 BCE.

region.text: the last Great Yuan shape, the Ferghana valley

ledger.note: 50: Cliopatria's Great Yuan row ends and the Kushan shape of 51 covers Ferghana. The Kangju page says the Hanshu (206 BCE-23 CE) has Kangju in 'control of Dayuan and Sogdiana' without a date; the Kushan page opened has no Ferghana. Page silent on the year and the taker; 50 is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: War of the Heavenly Horses

zones.text: Yucheng and Ershi, the Ferghana valley

wars.outcome: Han victory: after a 40-day siege of the capital the nobles killed King Wugua and gave Li Guangli about 3,000 horses; a pro-Han king, Meicai, was enthroned and Dayuan became a puppet state of Han. More than a year later the nobles killed Meicai and enthroned Wugua's brother Chanfeng, who sent his son as hostage, and the Han made peace.
wars.note: First expedition autumn 104 BC beaten at Yucheng; second autumn 102 to 101 BC. Wusun cavalry, 2,000 strong, were present 'at the request of Emperor Wu' but 'refused to take part in the siege'; Kangju sheltered the king of Yucheng and, per the Kangju page, allied with Dayuan in 101 BCE. The Dayuan page dates the Han expedition 104 BCE and 'By 100 BC' the defeat.

certainty.note: A small oasis kingdom in a mountain basin: the pages give no frontier, only cities and neighbours by direction (Kangju to the north-west, the Wusun and Yuezhi beyond).

notes: Not the Mongol Yuan: Cliopatria's 'Great Yuan' (-110..50, Ferghana valley) is Dayuan (Chinese 大宛), 'Yuan' being a transliteration of Yavana/Yona on the Dayuan page. Its Wikipedia field ('Yuan dynasty') and Wikidata id Q7313 belong to the Mongol Yuan dynasty (yuan-dynasty, great-mongol-state) and are wrong for this row; the dossier names the Dayuan article and leaves wikidata null because the Dayuan id is not in the tables (the gazetteer or colour agent should replace Q7313 in polities.csv). The three rows are different states. Added/changed: the state is drawn from -128 (Zhang Qian's account) instead of -110; this overlaps Cliopatria's Yuezhi shape of -126..-111, which contains the whole Ferghana basin: the yuezhi dossier (ia-01-a) does not mention it and should drop Ferghana from those years. The end in 50 is unverified; Cliopatria's Kushan 51 shape covers the basin, the Kangju page (Hanshu) has Kangju in control of Dayuan at an undated time before 23 CE. For other dossiers: the han-dynasty dossier (ea-02) should carry the vassal tint over Dayuan from 101 BC ('puppet-state of Han'; counterpart great-yuan) and its contest of -102 to -101. States needing dossiers: Kangju (neighbour to the north-west; controlled Dayuan at some point per the Hanshu), Saka of Ferghana (c. 160 BCE, Dayuan page, uncertain). Not settled: the capital (Guishan, Khujand or Ershi), the dates after 100 BC (page has none). Page budget: four pages of five. Gazetteer: all names resolve ('Fergana' is a region).
